__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Prometheus datasource that scrapes the Fred backends.

title: Fred / Platform health
description: Failed chat turns and backend HTTP errors, latency and traffic.

list.name: error_rate_24h
list.label: 24h error rate
list.description: Show the rolling 24-hour curves on both error-rate charts.

list.name: error_rate_detail
list.label: Error rate detail
list.description: Show the adaptive-window curves on both error-rate charts.

panels.title: Failed turns
panels.description: Failed turns divided by all recorded turns over the selected time range.

panels.title: HTTP 5xx
panels.description: 5xx responses divided by all HTTP requests across services over the selected time range.

panels.title: HTTP p95 latency
panels.description: p95 time until the API starts responding for 2xx/3xx requests, pooled across services over the selected time range.

panels.title: HTTP traffic
panels.description: Total estimated HTTP requests divided by the duration of the selected time range. The total is shown below.

panels.title: Failed turn rate over time
panels.description: Failed turns divided by all turns. The 24h error rate and Error rate detail controls show the rolling 24-hour and adaptive windows, respectively. Gaps indicate no recorded turns in the window or missing telemetry.

panels.title: Turn volume over time
panels.description: Estimated turn counts in each rolling hour. The total includes failed turns.

panels.title: Failed turn rate by agent template
panels.description: Failed turn rate for each catalog template over Grafana's adaptive rolling window. Check turn volume before interpreting a spike.

panels.title: Turn volume by agent template
panels.description: Estimated turn counts in each rolling hour for each catalog template.

panels.title: HTTP 5xx rate by service
panels.description: 5xx responses divided by all requests for each service. Solid lines use Grafana's adaptive window. Dashed lines use a rolling 24-hour window. Gaps indicate no requests in the window or missing samples.

targets.expr: (((sum by (service) (rate(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",http_status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval]))) or 0 * (sum by (service) (rate(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__rate_interval])))) / ((sum by (service) (rate(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__rate_interval]))) > 0)) and on () (vector(${error_rate_detail:raw}) == 1)

(((sum by (service) (rate(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",http_status=~"5.."}[24h]))) or 0 * (sum by (service) (rate(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}[24h])))) / ((sum by (service) (rate(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}[24h]))) > 0)) and on () (vector(${error_rate_24h:raw}) == 1)

panels.title: HTTP p95 latency by service
panels.description: Time until the API starts responding for 2xx/3xx requests. Stream completion is measured separately by chat turn telemetry.

panels.title: HTTP requests by endpoint
panels.description: Totals and p95 over the selected time range. Drag across a chart to focus on a spike. Sorted by 5xx requests. Latency covers 2xx/3xx responses.

targets.expr: ((sum by (service, method, route) (increase(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",http_status=~"5.."}[$__range]))) or 0 * (sum by (service, method, route) (increase(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__range])))) and ((sum by (service, method, route) (increase(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__range]))) > 0)

((sum by (service, method, route) (increase(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",http_status=~"5.."}[$__range]))) or 0 * (sum by (service, method, route) (increase(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__range])))) / ((sum by (service, method, route) (increase(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__range]))) > 0)

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service, method, route) (increase(api_request_latency_ms_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",http_status=~"[23].."}[$__range]))) and on (service, method, route) ((sum by (service, method, route) (increase(api_request_latency_ms_count{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__range]))) > 0)

panels.title: HTTP requests per second by service
panels.description: Requests observed by Fred backend middleware across all HTTP status codes.

panels.title: HTTP p95 latency by route
panels.description: Each line shows p95 time until the API starts responding for one service, HTTP method, and route. Uses 2xx/3xx responses and Grafana's adaptive window. Gaps indicate no successful requests in the window or missing telemetry.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service, method, route) (rate(api_request_latency_ms_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",http_status=~"[23].."}[$__rate_interval]))) >= 0
